 Golf instruction, social media trends and professional sports commentary featured in the October 22, 2026, edition of Screencaps, a daily column published by Fox News. The installment highlighted Paige Spiranac and former Peloton instructor Kendall Toole demonstrating golf techniques while also examining family activities, restaurant experiences and recent developments in baseball and women's basketball.
 Spiranac's golf content has shifted toward a more casual presentation, with the golf influencer appearing alongside a playing partner. The column credited this approach with attracting greater attention by emphasizing humor, playful exchanges and practical golf instruction rather than relying primarily on costumes.
 Advertisement 
 Scroll To Continue with Content 
 Toole, who previously worked as an instructor for Peloton, joined Spiranac in the golf demonstration. Their video offered viewers a step-by-step lesson on how to tee up a golf ball.

 Bill Murray Explores Ireland in Six Part Golf Documentary 
 A social media user identified as Rich responded to the content with a humorous remark about golf posture.
 "Good girls bend at the knee, bad girls bend at the hip . . . Or something like that . . . might be the other way round," Rich wrote on Instagram.
 The column also discussed so-called dump dinners, a style of family activity in which parents allow children to participate in messy food-related experiences. The writer questioned whether these activities primarily provide entertainment for young children or serve as material for parents to share on social media.
 Also Read 
 Sydney Sweeney Recreates Home Alone for Syrn Holiday Campaign 
 The discussion presented both possibilities, noting that messy activities could be enjoyable for toddlers while also raising questions about the role of online engagement in family life.
 Food quality emerged as another topic in the reader mailbag. A reader identified as Kevin F., from Naples, Florida, argued that nachos should be difficult for restaurants to prepare poorly. The columnist disagreed, pointing to inconsistent preparation and the practice of simply melting shredded cheese over tortilla chips.
 The exchange highlighted the difference between a basic serving of chips and cheese and a properly prepared plate of nachos. The column's discussion centered on restaurant execution rather than the complexity of the dish itself.
 Also Read 
 Donnie Iris Dies at 83 After Three Year Cancer Battle 
 Another reader described a positive experience at a Wendy's drive-through, where an older employee provided smooth service. The reader suggested that the encounter represented a welcome change from previous experiences.
 "Lo and behold!" the reader wrote when describing the unexpected sight of the employee at the drive-through window.
 The column also touched on Major League Baseball and the Women's National Basketball Association. One reader discussed the American League Championship Series and World Series, expressing support for Tampa Bay and criticizing the atmosphere at the team's stadium compared with American Family Field in Milwaukee.
 Also Read 
 Walter Koenig Dies at 90 After Playing Chekov in Star Trek 
 In women's basketball, the column raised questions about officiating during a WNBA Finals game between Atlanta and GSV. The writer highlighted a reported difference of 15 free throws in favor of Atlanta and questioned the league's broader promotional priorities. The commentary reflected the author's opinion rather than an independently established finding about officiating.
 Additional reader submissions covered fast-food buffets, restaurant service and memories of watching afternoon Chicago Cubs games. Together, the topics illustrated the column's recurring format of combining sports discussion with reader correspondence and everyday lifestyle observations.
